destination.name: Morton National Park
destination.tagline: Waterfall lookouts and gorges in the Southern Highlands and Shoalhaven escarpment.
destination.description: Morton National Park covers 199,745 hectares of the Southern Highlands, South Coast and Illawarra, about 170 km south-southwest of Sydney. NPWS describes imposing gorges alongside pockets of rainforest, with picnic areas and lookouts. The visitor base is Fitzroy Falls, where a boardwalk leads to a fall of 81 m into Yarrunga Valley, and the enclosed Kangaroo Valley lies close by with its 1898 suspension bridge.
whyVisit: See Fitzroy Falls from the boardwalk
Look over Kangaroo Valley from Belmore Falls

goodToKnow.title: Fitzroy Falls has an entry fee
goodToKnow.detail: The Fitzroy Falls lookout is listed at about $4 entry; the Fitzroy Falls Visitor Centre is the park base. Check NPWS for current fees.

goodToKnow.title: Belmore Falls base is closed
goodToKnow.detail: The walking track gives lookouts over Kangaroo Valley and the falls, but the base of the falls is permanently closed.

goodToKnow.title: Bring a car
goodToKnow.detail: Kangaroo Valley has no train service; a bus links Nowra and Moss Vale, and Wikivoyage names a car as the best way to reach the sights away from the village.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} bring mild weather for lookout walks, avoiding the heat of summer.
